chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran ad-Daqaq, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-San'ani, and Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Mokattib - may God have mercy upon them - narrated that Abul Husayn Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi, on the authority of Sahl ibn Zayd al-Adami, on the authority of Abdul Adheem ibn Abdullah al-Hasani, on the authority of Mahmud ibn Abi al-Bilad, said: I heard the Imam (peace be upon him) say:
Whoever is not grateful to the bestower of blessings from among the created beings is not grateful to God, the Mighty and Exalted.

key_terms.الْمُنْعِمَ: the bestower of blessings / the benefactor

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between being grateful to people and being grateful to God in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* underscores the Shia concept of *Shukr al-Ni'mah* by linking vertical gratitude to God with horizontal appreciation of His agents. It implies that created beings are not independent sources of blessing but rather channels (*wasila*) of divine grace, making gratitude to them a necessary component of thanking the Ultimate Bestower. This principle reinforces the interconnectedness of divine sovereignty and human social ethics in Shia jurisprudence and theology.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-2 Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Imran ad-Daqaq, Muhammad ibn Ahmad Al-San’ani and Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad al-Mokattib - may God have mercy upon them - narrated that Abul Husayn Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi quoted on the authority of Sahl ibn Zayd al-Adami, on the authority of Abdul Adheem ibn Abdullah Al-Hassani, on the authority of Mahmood ibn Abil Bilad that he had heard Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) say, “
Whoever is ungrateful for the blessings from the created ones is not grateful to God the Honorable the Exalted.”
